**Colossians 1**

*Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timotheus our brother,*

*2 To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.*

*3 We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you,*

*4 Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love which ye have to all the saints,*

*5 For the hope which is laid up for you in heaven, whereof ye heard before in the word of the truth of the gospel;*

*6 Which is come unto you, as it is in all the world; and bringeth forth fruit, as it doth also in you, since the day ye heard of it, and knew the grace of God in truth:*

*7 As ye also learned of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ;*

*8 Who also declared unto us your love in the Spirit.*

*9 For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;*

*10 That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;*

*11 Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness;*

*12 Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light:*

*13 Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son:*

*14 In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins:*

*15 Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature:*

*16 For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:*

*17 And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.*

*18 And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.*

*19 For it pleased the Father that in him should all fulness dwell;*

*20 And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven.*

*21 And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled*

*22 In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight:*

*23 If ye continue in the faith grounded and settled, and be not moved away from the hope of the gospel, which ye have heard, and which was preached to every creature which is under heaven; whereof I Paul am made a minister;*

*24 Who now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his body's sake, which is the church:*

*25 Whereof I am made a minister, according to the dispensation of God which is given to me for you, to fulfil the word of God;*

*26 Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints:*

*27 To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory:*

*28 Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom; that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus:*

*29 Whereunto I also labour, striving according to his working, which worketh in me mightily.*

Here in the opening of Paul's letter to the saints at Colosse, we have one of the most eloquent descriptions of who Jesus is and our shared faith in Him.

Note again, Paul prays for God's grace, and the peace that comes from it for those reading. It is only possible to have peace by having peace with God, and that peace is only possible by being partakers of His grace. And all knowledge and wisdom of God's word comes from Him, and those sincerely seeking it. Paul wishes all this that the Colossians may continue being fruitful, sharing the faith and winning more to the body of the church, which is Christ's. Preached to every creature.

Strengthened with His glorious power, that we may endure all things with longsuffering and patience and joy. Delivered with His blood. Redeemed by Him. Partakers of the inheritance of the light, saved from the darkness. Translated into the Kingdom of Heaven.

(This is the biblical meaning of being translated in regards to our spiritual state, and the Kingdom. It is not the bodily assumption of our corruptible flesh, as some presume, but a change of our spirit, quickened by the Holy Ghost, made acceptable by the blood)

Jesus is the express image of God the Father, and made through Jesus, all that has been created is His, who was before all things. Who is the first fruits of the resurrection, so that He may have preeminence in even that, making peace with God through the cross, reconciling all things.

And for us who are grounded and settled to this Gospel of reconciliation:

*And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled. In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight.*

We who were dead in sin, enemies of God through our wicked works, made unblameable and unreproveable before God, reconciled with the Father by the Son. Our sins forever forgiven.

And Paul made a minister unto the Gentiles, suffering in the flesh for the Gospel's sake, to edify, build up, the body which is the congregation of believers, serving the head which is Christ Jesus. Rejoicing in this suffering, Paul encourages us with this joy, that we may preach to every man and win every man to the same peace we have through grace in Christ.

**Colossians 2**

*For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;*

*2 That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ;*

*3 In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.*

*4 And this I say, lest any man should beguile you with enticing words.*

*5 For though I be absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit, joying and beholding your order, and the stedfastness of your faith in Christ.*

*6 As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him:*

*7 Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving.*

*8 Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.*

*9 For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.*

*10 And ye are complete in him, which is the head of all principality and power:*

*11 In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ:*

*12 Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead.*

*13 And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, hath he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses;*

*14 Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross;*

*15 And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.*

*16 Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days:*

*17 Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.*

*18 Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,*

*19 And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God.*

*20 Wherefore if ye be dead with Christ from the rudiments of the world, why, as though living in the world, are ye subject to ordinances,*

*21 (Touch not; taste not; handle not;*

*22 Which all are to perish with the using;) after the commandments and doctrines of men?*

*23 Which things have indeed a shew of wisdom in will worship, and humility, and neglecting of the body: not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh.*

Paul continues his greeting to the churches in Colosse, including a shout out to the early church in Laodicea, churches he himself didn't establish in person, as the Gospel has been preached throughout the world, faith to faith, to the Gentiles, beyond even Paul's direct ministry.

All believers, members of the body of which Jesus is the head, united in spirit, in the joy of peace with God through grace and faith, sharing the goal of bringing increase, the harvest of fruit of righteousness, winning souls to Christ with the Gospel of reconciliation. Bringing forth fruit meet for repentance. Turning those that heard and believe towards God.

We see in epistle after epistle, in the Acts of the apostles, in Jesus' own ministry, and His sending of disciples out, two by two into the highways and hedges. We see it in John the Baptist's preaching in the wilderness. It is faith shared and souls won. To God the increase.

The so called holy men, vipers chastised by John and Jesus Himself, Peter and Paul, were unable to bring forth this fruit, to lead believers to Christ.

Neither can false prophets, and yet they are here in Colosse as they were in Galatia, Ephesus, in the Judean wilderness, as Satan himself, trying to lead the churches astray, causing others to sin, and damning souls with their doctrines of works.

It's the same play as Satan in the desert with Christ. We see it today. They beguile us with enticing words, to *spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.*

Paul is again writing to warn the churches of the Judaizers, who were demanding a return to Hebrew roots by the newly grafted Gentiles, adherence to the Law, the carnal ordinances and the circumcision of the flesh. The acts and works and vain traditions of men, dietary laws, esteeming days over others, all done away with in Christ as they were a foreshadowing of Him.

This is told to us, over and over again, because it is Satan's main play against us. Giant red flags that should warn us of false preachers who creep in among us to lead some astray. It is the bulk of the NT outside the Gospel by which we are saved for a reason. Even moreso than instruction against sin, Paul and James and Peter and Jude write to warn the churches to avoid these doctrines of men and appeal to the flesh, and remind us we are of a spiritual circumcision.

**Colossians 3** 

*If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.*

*2 Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.*

*3 For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God.*

*4 When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory.*

*5 Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry:*

*6 For which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience:*

*7 In the which ye also walked some time, when ye lived in them.*

*8 But now ye also put off all these; anger, wrath, malice, blasphemy, filthy communication out of your mouth.*

*9 Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds;*

*10 And have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him:*

*11 Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free: but Christ is all, and in all.*

*12 Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering;*

*13 Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.*

*14 And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.*

*15 And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.*

*16 Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.*

*17 And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.*

*18 Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as it is fit in the Lord.*

*19 Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them.*

*20 Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord.*

*21 Fathers, provoke not your children to anger, lest they be discouraged.*

*22 Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God;*

*23 And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men;*

*24 Knowing that of the Lord ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance: for ye serve the Lord Christ.*

*25 But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons.*

Paul's focus shifts to now-familiar themes. If we be saved, children of light, then seek the things of Heaven. The word of God. The glory of Jesus. The resurrection to come and being raptured, caught up, into the clouds with Him in glory.

For this cause, we should mortify our members against sin of the flesh, even as Jesus preached (later in today's Matthew study), "if an eye offend thee, pluck it out." We who are heirs keep our bodies in submission and our thoughts to what's pure, good and holy.

Lusts of the flesh, lust, which is the longing for what's not yours, worshiping in the Idolatry of covetousness. As it is written, in **James 4**:

*From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members? Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not. Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.*

These sins are the reason for God's wrath upon the children of disobedience to the Gospel, but we are children of the light, the shining city in the hill. The light we have inside is a reflection and magnifying of the love God shines on us, so don't hide it, but hold it high for all to see that they might be partakers with us. Putting off anger, wrath,Malice, blasphemy, filthy conversation, the behavior of the unsaved that acts as a bushel to hide our light and turn some away from the truth within us.

We put on the new man, have honest dealings with one another ("Let your yea be yea, and your nay, nay" - also Matt 5), doing everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, in thanks to God the Father by Christ's name.

And if we are in the new man, and we have put away the lusts of the flesh, if we mortify our members, having honest dealings with one another, edifying with songs of praise and teaching the doctrines of God in psalms, our light shining as a guide to the truth for others to follow, then what does this look like?

Wives submitting to their husbands, husbands loving their wives, children honoring their parents, fathers judging their children righteously,not in wrath, not frustrating them, but as God the Father has loved you.

And, at work? Heartily and without malice or anger, do what you're asked, because we work for God, already rewarded with the kingdom of which we are heirs. Diligently and honestly setting out to complete what is required of you, with joy and a meek spirit and the confidence of your salvation.

Those who do wrong will have their reward, just as you will for your faithful service. God is not a respecter of persons, and master or boss or elected leader, all alike will face His wrath for their transgressions. That's not on us to determine. It is on us to account for ourselves in all that we do, because we do it in Jesus' name.

Many bristle at this. Be the best husband, wife, child, employee, neighbor, regardless of whatever else. Being blameless. Not dimming the reflection of the light that you walk in. *If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.*

So many struggle with this concept. Some false prophets and natural men claim that this submission to authority and the powers that be, given by God, as some sort of perversion by Paul, but we see it again in **Matthew 5**, preached by Jesus in the beatitudes. A study on that will be posted hopefully this afternoon. Working 12hr days lately

**Colossians 3**
*If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.*

*2 Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.*

*3 For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God.*

*4 When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory.*

*5 Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry:*

*6 For which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience:*

*7 In the which ye also walked some time, when ye lived in them.*

*8 But now ye also put off all these; anger, wrath, malice, blasphemy, filthy communication out of your mouth.*

*9 Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds;*

*10 And have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him:*

*11 Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free: but Christ is all, and in all.*

*12 Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering;*

*13 Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.*

*14 And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.*

*15 And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.*

*16 Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.*

*17 And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.*

**Romans 7**
*14 For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.*

*15 For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.*

*16 If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.*

*17 Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.*

*18 For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not.*

*19 For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do.*

*20 Now if I do that I would not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.*

I would that all who believe on Christ for salvation come to the understanding that, as befitting a quickened spirit, a new man, we put off the lusts of the flesh and put on the things of God. Mortifying our members, being dead to sin.

But as Paul explains, this isn't automatic. It isn't even a necessity to salvation, as he is writing we who are saved by faith in Christ.

And because it is not automatic, and yet our new man cries out for us to be holy, many men take advantage of this conflict, warning within our members. They come with philosophy and vain deceit; that is the ideas of men that claim to know truth, often that is hidden, that doesn't come from scripture. Or from traditions of men, that things that come from the vain beliefs, and are adopted as religious practices, must be followed. These things aren't of Christ.

Christ in whom we not only have died with and been quickened, and redeemed, our sins done away with and the ordinances taken away. Nailed to His cross.

Therefore, we should not allow any man to judge us in meat, or in drink, or in respect to an holiday, or new moon, or sabbath, all of which were shadows of Christ, or any other condition that they teach for doctrine that are commandments of men and offered in their place.

This means that the vain philosophy of men, as well as the old testament strictures, have no power over we who are saved by faith in Christ. And men who place these things as stumbling blocks and snares are attempting to beguile us. Trapping us into things like voluntary humility, that is sackcloth and ashes. Self-flagellation. Aestheticism, the denial of self for the purpose of self-righteousness (*Touch not; taste not; handle not; Which all are to perish with the using)*.

Weird doctrines like the worship of angels (or saints). Things that they haven't seen themselves, but imagine in their fleshly mind. Things other than Christ who is the head of us who are saved.

Don't be misled by people who indeed seem holy, who may be able to make an argument of men in the wisdom of how they worship in their humility and neglecting things of the body. Unsaved and even reprobates, can fast for example. They may live without gluttony or abstaining from alcohol. They may be even living "cleaner" than some saved Christians. They may refuse to celebrate certain holidays or feasts, citing earthly reasons and the denial of themselves as a form of righteousness. But these are all lies and not of Christ, in whom is liberty.

Chapter 3 goes into details of how a saved Christian *should* seek to clean up their lives. These things that should be done because we are free in Christ and dead to the flesh. Not because man tells us to. Not to show our own holiness but to put off these deeds as new creatures, not beholden to the things of the flesh. But renewed in the knowledge of Christ, as the elect of God. Using the wisdom of His doctrines to teach and rebuke one another. Giving thanks to God through Christ Jesus.

It is the subtle difference between legalism and rejoicing that we are free in grace. And discernment is required.

And here's the thing. I don't just pronounce things as doctrine. I lay out in a methodical way the scripture that I'm depending on for doctrine. I go verse by verse chapter by chapter book by book through the Bible; including posting nearly every other relevant reference and passage, so that there can be no misunderstanding what I believe.

And while someone doesn't have to agree with all of the conclusions that I've made, They have to admit that they're done from scripture and that they are done in good faith, hiding nothing.

**Colossians 4**

*Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal; knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.*

*2 Continue in prayer, and watch in the same with thanksgiving;*

*3 Withal praying also for us, that God would open unto us a door of utterance, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in bonds:*

*4 That I may make it manifest, as I ought to speak.*

*5 Walk in wisdom toward them that are without, redeeming the time.*

*6 Let your speech be always with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.*

*7 All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, who is a beloved brother, and a faithful minister and fellowservant in the Lord:*

*8 Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that he might know your estate, and comfort your hearts;*

*9 With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They shall make known unto you all things which are done here.*

*10 Aristarchus my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Marcus, sister's son to Barnabas, (touching whom ye received commandments: if he come unto you, receive him;)*

*11 And Jesus, which is called Justus, who are of the circumcision. These only are my fellowworkers unto the kingdom of God, which have been a comfort unto me.*

*12 Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.*

*13 For I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis.*

*14 Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas, greet you.*

*15 Salute the brethren which are in Laodicea, and Nymphas, and the church which is in his house.*

*16 And when this epistle is read among you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans; and that ye likewise read the epistle from Laodicea.*

*17 And say to Archippus, Take heed to the ministry which thou hast received in the Lord, that thou fulfil it.*

*18 The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.*

The final chapter of Colossians, the first verse of which is really the last of the though carried in Chapter 3. Everyone is subject to the Lord, and has a master in heaven. The powers that be are to be honored and feared, and not to be abused should you be husband, master, minister, bishop. Being not a respecter of persons, as God is not. Loving our enemies, rejoicing in the Spirit.

And so, continue in prayer, thanksgiving, praying God brings opportunities to share His Gospel with others. The mystery of Christ which the preaching of had Paul in chains. He asks for prayers that he be able to deliver the same to those who held him captive and this magnify the Lord.

He encourages us to walk in wisdom towards those who lack it, making the best use of our limited time.

Speaking with grace seasoned with salt. This is a skill that comes from being in the word and reflecting on the grace God has shown us. It is speaking the truth in love and understanding. Being longsuffering, but not afraid to say what God's word says. To speak what He's spoken unto us. Not in malice or spite, but with understanding of the human condition of the unregenerate sinners we interact with, that some might be saved. It can be hard sometimes, at least for me, but the reward that comes from it is most excellent.

Paul concludes this epistle, (hand written himself whereas some were transcribed) with shout-outs to many fellow ministers who did great things for God. Luke, that author of the Gospel and Acts is mentioned. Barnabas' nephew. Paul is always ready to give credit to the many who labored in the Gospel with him, as we should be generous to praise the good work of others, and name them. God being just and true gave them the honor of being known throughout the ages.

Paul asks that this epistle be also delivered unto the church at Laodicea, and an epistle delivered there to be read in Colosse. Would love to read this "lost letter." Although, some believe that the letter to Philemon is this epistle, some scholars debate whether it was simply another that was redundant to known epistles, going over similar themes and using similar language.

History shows multiple forgeries we're attempted in the early days of the 2nd century. Like any book mentioned in the Bible but not reproduced, Satan leaps at the chance to introduce blasphemy with the implied authority of being mentioned in scripture.

Of course Laodicea is one of the churches Jesus addresses in Revelation 3, the lukewarm church that lost it's fire for the gospel in the comfort of the material wealth they had, who Christ calls to repent unto zeal or see the church lost.
